raw_response:
My land is about 8 mu here in Quzhou. My father grew wheat and corn on this same ground, and I have grown wheat and corn my whole life. I know this land. I know when the rains come and when they don't. I see no reason to change.

Come October I will sow winter wheat again — I will use the improved seed from the township supply cooperative, same as last few years, it does better than the old varieties. I will rotary till first to break up the maize stubble, then sow. Before sowing I mix in the basal fertilizer — compound fertilizer plus urea. I will irrigate four times: before sowing to settle the soil, again before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll spray twice — once in spring for aphids, once if I see powdery mildew coming on.

After wheat harvest in June, I will plant summer maize directly into the stubble, no tillage — saves my back and my diesel money. I use hybrid seed, everyone does now, the yield is better. I will top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. Irrigation once or twice depending on rain. One spray for corn borer if I need it.

I am 68, my knees are not good. I hire a neighbor's tractor for the rotary tilling and a machine for wheat harvest. I do the seeding and spraying myself. My wife helps.
